samples.marker_note: VB6 disk binder worm: separate layout facts from hostile behavior
samples.identification: ASPack-packed native VB6 disk binder, file infector and drive autorun worm
evidence: Unpacked ASPack using Unicorn with stubbed allocator and loader APIs; control returns at VA 0x4014d8 after 1258560 emulated instructions. No native execution or network access.

Recovered native VB6 routines read file records at 0x403310/0x4033f0 and rewrite two records with __vbaPutOwner3 and __vbaPutOwner4 at 0x4035bb/0x4035d7. Form routines select *.exe and carry their own body and host data.

At 0x40451a a drive-root autorun.inf is opened for output; 0x404549 and 0x40455b print [Autorun] and Shell=NTDETECT.EXE. Following code copies the image to the matching drive-root NTDETECT.EXE and sets attributes.
0x403a59 creates WScript.Shell, then 0x403b05 invokes Regwrite with an HKLM CurrentVersion Run value pointing to the staged executable. This is incompatible with the Microsoft Firewall identity.

The outer file contains many PE images, including ordinary Java tooling. Their presence alone establishes neither execution nor malicious intent. The raw packed scan now retains two suspicious findings; the malicious verdict rests on recovered code.

samples.marker_note: StormAttack injector: require self-copy patch code for Active Setup
samples.identification: Damaged memory-dump variant of a native StormAttack service/DLL injector
evidence: Both variants have byte-identical .text (file offsets 0x1000..0x3000). Entry CRT calls 0x401cb0. Mode 3 calls 0x401900 then self-delete 0x401390; alternate modes configure service loading or inject a DLL.
0x401900 constructs a GUID-named Active Setup key and writes StubPath, reads the current image via CRT I/O, edits its mode and path fields, saves a copy, and starts it with CreateProcessA.

0x401afe clears eight dwords, 0x401b0e tags the first byte, and 0x401b26 writes the buffer. The new instruction trait varies stack/IAT addresses and the tag; the Active Setup objective additionally requires module-path I/O, fwrite and the proven injector/service-hijack context.

0x401150 chooses IE/notepad/calc, calls CreateProcessA, VirtualAllocEx and WriteProcessMemory, resolves kernel32!LoadLibraryA and supplies that export and remote DLL path to CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d.
0x401260 replaces HKLM SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters ServiceDLL with a staged DLL path. 0x402460 extracts DLL resource 101 and 0x4023c0 writes the extracted bytes.
0x401390 obtains its module path, converts to 8.3 form, obtains COMSPEC, builds /c del <self> > nul and starts a shell. These are code paths, not proof of successful runtime installation.
The dumped headers, bound IAT contents and hardcoded original file offsets are damaged. Do not claim that the specimens install or run their payloads successfully.
samples.payload: Resource at 0x5060 is a 39936-byte PE DLL with about 94.5% zero bytes; strings/configuration survive but import table, code and exports are erased. No DDoS or network-execution claim is made from its strings.

changes: Moved ASPack/writable-entry/embedded-PE/majority-overlay co-occurrence into metadata/binary/layout/overlay at notable; preserved its conditions and scope.
Removed redundant packing/layout composites that added unsupported decoy, dynamic-loader or concealed-payload claims; their constituent metadata/API facts remain visible.

Canonicalized the Microsoft Firewall label under vendor metadata and removed Firewall.exe as interchangeable evidence of a Microsoft claim. Moved the Xiang company-name reference to version provenance and updated exact consumers.
Kept packed Firewall/Xiang contradiction suspicious, independent of the recovered malicious behavior.
Added a section-scoped native buffer-clear/tag/call instruction trait and required it plus fwrite for Active Setup injector persistence.
controls: Positive: both StormAttack targets match the new instruction sequence and retain four hostile traits across evasion, login persistence, service persistence and family identity.
Near miss: changing the eight-dword clear count from 8 to 7 removes the new instruction match and refined Active Setup objective, while independent service/injection detections remain.
Inert ret-only ASPack-labeled writable-entry PE with an ordinary Java PE overlay matches relocated layout metadata at notable and produces no hostile finding.
external_sources: Supplied triage report URLs were inaccessible; no external verdict or filename family label was used as proof.
